examName: Bocconi University Admissions Requirements (Undergraduate / Law / Master of Science)
versionLabel: Bocconi admissions — a.y. 2027-28 cycle (primary, currently published) with a.y. 2026-27 cycle retained where still live
region: Italy (Milan); applicants worldwide, separate Italian / international booking windows
admissionsCycle: Two cycles in scope. (1) a.y. 2026-27 — applications ran Sept 2025 to Apr 2026; still live on the site for results/enrollment and for the online-test rules-of-conduct PDF. (2) a.y. 2027-28 — the cycle actually open on 2026-09-18: Bachelor/Law Early Session 2-29 September 2026; MSc Round I 1-29 October 2026. As of the verification date Bocconi had NOT published a 2027-28 rules-of-conduct PDF; only the 2026-27 edition exists.
deliveryMode: Online Bocconi test: remote, at-home, proctored. Candidate's own computer plus a second mobile device as a side camera; Safe Exam Browser lockdown browser; identity check with photo ID; 360-degree room scan; continuous audio/video recording reviewed after submission. SAT / ACT / LSAT / GMAT / GRE are delivered by their own test makers and Bocconi only consumes the score report (GRE General Test at Home is NOT accepted by Bocconi).
summary: Bocconi admissions requirements are strictly stratified by school and level, and a single "Bocconi requirements" model would be wrong. For Bachelor (Undergraduate School) programs Bocconi accepts the Online Bocconi test, SAT or ACT; for Law School programs (Integrated Master of Arts in Law and Bachelor in Global Law) it additionally accepts the LSAT and a separate "Online Bocconi test - Law" with a different blueprint. For Master of Science it accepts GMAT, GRE or a third, graduate-specific Online Bocconi test. Every number Bocconi publishes is an ELIGIBILITY FLOOR ("will not be considered"), never a competitive or expected admitted score: SAT 1040 total and 520 per section, ACT composite 19, LSAT 147, Online Bocconi test 17/50 (undergraduate and law) or 15/50 (graduate), GMAT Exam 500/800 or GMAT Focus Edition 485/805. Bocconi publishes no average or median admitted scores on the pages verified; admission is by ranking (undergraduate: test 55% / GPA 45%) against a fixed number of places, and English certification is required only at enrollment, not at selection.
totalQuestions: Online Bocconi test (all three variants): 50 multiple-choice questions. SAT/ACT/LSAT/GMAT/GRE question counts are governed by their own test makers and are out of scope for this admissions-requirements task.
totalTimeMinutes: 75 (Online Bocconi test, all three variants: undergraduate, law, graduate)
timingAndBreaks: The Online Bocconi test lasts 75 minutes as a single continuous block. There are no per-section time limits and no published per-area timing: Bocconi explicitly states questions are "distributed within the test in a mixed way both by difficulty level and by topic" and that candidates must manage their own time. No scheduled breaks are published, and the 2026-27 rules of conduct prohibit "leaving once the test has started". The candidate may sit the test at any time between 12:00am and 11:59pm (CET/CEST) on the booked day. The test closes automatically when time expires and answers are saved and submitted. Candidates with disabilities or specific learning disorders may be granted additional time, applied via a code entered when purchasing the attempt, following a request submitted at least 5 working days before the test date.
navigationAndReview: Strictly forward-only, in blocks of three. The 2026-27 official rules state: "The test offers 3 questions for each screen. With the 'Next' button, you can view the next screen but going back to the previous one will no longer be possible." There is a "test navigation" box on every page acting as a guide. Skipping forward without answering is permitted but irreversible, and Bocconi warns that clicking through all questions forfeits any refund or discount of the attempt. To finish, the candidate clicks "Finish attempt", which shows a summary page listing all questions answered and unanswered, then "Submit all and finish". That summary is a review-of-status screen only — the forward-only rule means prior answers cannot be revisited or changed. Time expiry forces submission. No flagging/bookmarking feature is documented. SAT, ACT, LSAT, GMAT and GRE navigation rules are set by their own test makers, not by Bocconi.
calculatorRules: No calculator of any kind is permitted on the Online Bocconi test. The 2026-27 rules of conduct forbid "having books, notebooks, notes, formularies, calculators or sources/resources available online". The only permitted materials are the identification document, 1 pencil or pen (no more), 2 blank A4 sheets of paper, and a drink in an unlabelled container — all of which must be shown to the system on request. No on-screen calculator is documented. Calculator policy for SAT, ACT, GMAT and GRE is set by those test makers and must not be inherited from Bocconi's rules.
adaptiveBehavior: Not adaptive, and must not be simulated as adaptive. Bocconi publishes a fixed blueprint of exactly 50 questions with fixed per-area counts for each variant, a single 75-minute block, and forward-only sequential delivery in screens of three. No official Bocconi page verified in this session describes routing, module selection, difficulty branching, or ability estimation. Bocconi does state that "questions are distributed within the test in a mixed way both by difficulty level and by topic", which is fixed interleaving, not adaptivity. Whether Bocconi draws items from a pool with randomised assignment per candidate is not publicly documented.
scoringRawRules: Online Bocconi test — Undergraduate and Law variants: "Right answer: 1 point", "Missing answer: 0 points", "Wrong answer: - 0.2 points", with "- 0.33 points" applied instead to certain critical-thinking questions that have three options. Eligibility floor: "Applicants who receive a total score (penalties included) lower than 17 will not be considered in the selection process." Online Bocconi test — Graduate variant (International Graduate applicants): "Right answer: 1 point", "Missing answer: 0 points", "Wrong answer: -0.25/-0.33 points", with the floor at "lower than 15 out of 50". Omitted answers are never penalised in any variant, so the rational strategy differs from the SAT's no-penalty scoring — the engine must expose this. Raw score is out of 50. A score report is available in the candidate's personal area within 48 hours and breaks down the total, the per-area scores, and the counts of correct / unanswered / incorrect answers.
scoringScaleRules: There is no scaled score for the Online Bocconi test: the reported score is the raw penalty-adjusted total out of 50. For Bachelor and Law admission, the test score is one component of a ranking: "1. Selection test score - 55% ... 2. Third-last and second-last year GPA - 45%". Where a candidate submits more than one accepted test, "the online admission portal will pick the highest for you" (undergraduate) and for MSc "the system automatically considers the most competitive one" — but the mechanism by which scores on different scales (Bocconi 0-50, SAT 400-1600, ACT 1-36, LSAT 120-180) are made commensurable for ranking is NOT published. For MSc, admission rests on three compulsory elements — test score, undergraduate GPA/transcripts, and dossier/motivation evaluation — and "Applications will not be evaluated if any of these three elements are missing." Ranking is applied against a fixed number of places per round: "approximately 3000 places are available overall" for a.y. 2027-28.
scoringNotPubliclyDocumented: The concordance or normalisation used to compare candidates who submitted different tests (Online Bocconi test 0-50 vs SAT 400-1600 vs ACT 1-36 vs LSAT 120-180) into one ranking score. Bocconi says the portal picks the 'highest' / 'most competitive' result but publishes no conversion table.
How the 45% GPA component is normalised across different national secondary-school grading systems into a comparable value.
Item-level difficulty calibration, IRT parameters, or any statistical model behind the Online Bocconi test. No official page verified describes item calibration.
Whether items are drawn per candidate from a pool, and if so the pool size, exposure controls, or form-equating between attempts (candidates may take up to four attempts per academic year).
The actual admission cut-off rank score per program per round. This is a consequence of applicant volume and places available and is not published in advance.

The exact GRE combined Verbal+Quantitative threshold table used for MSc eligibility. The page states no minimum individual section score is set, but the combined-score values could not be extracted verbatim and reliably in this session.
Which specific critical-thinking question types carry the -0.33 penalty rather than -0.2 (Bocconi states only that it applies to certain three-option critical-thinking items).
Any percentile, score distribution, or admitted-student score statistic. Bocconi does not publish these on the pages verified.

skills: Mathematics (24 of 50 questions on the undergraduate blueprint)
Economic-topic passages (GDP, deficit, inflation) containing numbers, percentages and data that must be understood and analysed
Three-option critical-thinking items carrying the -0.33 wrong-answer penalty
Mathematics (5 questions on the law blueprint)
Discursive and humanistic passages: pedagogy, history, philosophy, geography
Logics and critical thinking (18 questions, the largest single area on the law blueprint)
Verbal reasoning (10 questions) - present on the law blueprint only, absent from the undergraduate blueprint

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief treats the platform's Bocconi coverage as 'Bocconi Online Test - undergraduate and law', implying two test variants.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: There are THREE distinct Online Bocconi test variants with different blueprints, penalties and eligibility floors: undergraduate (4 areas, -0.2/-0.33, floor 17, 4 attempts), law (5 areas including a Verbal reasoning area absent from the undergraduate form, floor 17, 4 attempts), and an International Graduate variant (3 areas - Verbal reasoning / Data insight / Quantitative reasoning, -0.25/-0.33, floor 15, 3 attempts).
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: The exam config registry needs three separate versioned Bocconi configs, not two. The graduate variant must not inherit the undergraduate penalty constant (-0.2 vs -0.25) or the attempt cap (4 vs 3), or scoring will be wrong for every graduate attempt.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief flags 'Claims presenting competitive admissions scores as official thresholds' as a risk to investigate.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: Confirmed and material. Every Bocconi number verified is an eligibility floor phrased 'will not be considered' (SAT 1040/520, ACT 19, LSAT 147, Bocconi test 17, graduate Bocconi test 15, GMAT 500 / Focus 485). Bocconi publishes no average, median or competitive admitted score on any page verified. Third-party sites circulate figures such as 'Bocconi SAT 1450+' which have no official basis.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Every score value in the content model must carry a mandatory enum field scoreClass: 'official-requirement' | 'historical-statistic'. The UI must render official-requirement values as 'minimum to be considered' and must refuse to render any historical-statistic without a visible non-official attribution. No admission-probability calculator, no 'your chances' widget, no score-to-likelihood mapping.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief flags 'Bocconi navigation, penalties, eligibility thresholds, and program-specific requirements' as needing investigation.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: All four verified. Navigation is strictly forward-only in screens of three questions with no return. Penalties are -0.2 (or -0.33 for three-option critical-thinking items) with zero for omissions. The eligibility floor is 17/50 including penalties. A program-specific requirement exists: Mathematical and Computing Sciences for AI additionally requires SAT Math 600/800 or ACT Math 25/36.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: The navigation model needs a 'blockForwardOnly' mode with blockSize=3 that is genuinely irreversible - not merely a hidden Back button. Because omissions cost nothing while wrong answers cost 0.2, the results screen must report omitted and incorrect counts separately and must not present raw percent-correct as the headline metric.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief lists 'GMAT - current format; accommodate searches using Focus Edition', implying Focus Edition is a search-alias for one current exam.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: For Bocconi admissions purposes these are two separately-scored exams that coexist: the GMAT Exam is scored out of 800 with a Bocconi minimum of 500, and the GMAT Focus Edition is scored out of 805 with a Bocconi minimum of 485. Both are simultaneously valid under the five-year score-validity rule.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: The Bocconi MSc requirements page must present two GMAT rows with different scales, not one. Treating Focus Edition as a synonym would produce a wrong eligibility check for anyone with a legacy 800-scale score.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief asks to 'keep undergraduate, law, and graduate admissions requirements clearly separated' but does not specify the axis of separation.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: The correct axis is SCHOOL, not just level. Bocconi builds separate rankings for the Undergraduate School and the Law School, and the accepted test set differs by school (LSAT and Online Bocconi test - Law are law-only, and the law test cannot be used for non-law programs). Graduate is a third, entirely separate track with different tests, a different document set, and four rounds instead of two.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Model the requirements entity keyed by (school, cycle) rather than by (level). A shared 'Bocconi undergraduate requirements' page that mixes law would state a false accepted-test list in both directions.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief implicitly assumes one current admissions cycle per exam.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: Two cycles are live simultaneously on unibocconi.it as of 2026-09-18. The Admissions page and MSc pages describe a.y. 2027-28 (Early Session open 2-29 September 2026), while the Timeline page and the Results and Enrollment page still describe a.y. 2026-27 (deadlines in 2025-2026, enrollment English deadline 30 June 2026). The rules-of-conduct PDF exists only in its 2026-27 edition.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: Every Bocconi fact record needs an explicit admissionsCycle field and a sourcePageCycle field, plus a verificationDate. The UI must label which cycle a deadline belongs to, otherwise learners will see a 2026 deadline presented as current. Build a staleness check that flags any Bocconi record whose cycle label is older than the currently-open application cycle.

briefDiscrepancies.briefClaim: The brief lists broad response-type support including quantitative comparison, data sufficiency, numeric entry, essay and two-part.
briefDiscrepancies.verifiedFinding: For Bocconi specifically, all three test variants are described solely as multiple-choice, and no essay, numeric-entry, quantitative-comparison or data-sufficiency response type is documented on any Bocconi page verified. Bocconi's undergraduate test is described as 'SAT-oriented' but that is a design-influence statement, not an adoption of SAT response types.
briefDiscrepancies.implementationConsequence: The Bocconi exam configs should enable only single_select (plus passage_group for the reading-comprehension items that share a stimulus). Those other response types are needed for other exams in the platform, not for Bocconi, and enabling them in a Bocconi config would produce content that does not resemble the real test.

implementationNotes: TIMING: single server-authoritative 75-minute deadline for all three Bocconi test configs. No per-section timers, no scheduled breaks. On expiry the server must auto-submit and persist whatever is answered, mirroring 'the test will close automatically when the available time has expired'. Accommodation support: an extendedTimeMultiplier hook exists in the real process (a code applied at purchase), so the config should expose an optional time multiplier but the platform must not invent a specific multiplier value because Bocconi does not publish one.

NAVIGATION: implement a navigationMode of 'forward-only-blocks' with blockSize=3 for all three Bocconi configs. Advancing must be a committed, irreversible server-side transition, not a client-side hidden Back button. Persist the pointer so a refresh or reconnect resumes at the same block and cannot rewind. Provide a final review screen that shows answered/unanswered status only, with answers locked, matching the real 'Finish attempt' summary followed by 'Submit all and finish'.

CALCULATOR: calculatorPolicy must be 'none' for all Bocconi configs, with no on-screen calculator rendered. Do not let a global default from the SAT or GMAT configs leak into the Bocconi configs. Present the permitted-materials list (ID, one pen, two blank A4 sheets, unlabelled drink) as exam-context guidance, clearly labelled as Bocconi's real-world rule rather than something the web app enforces.

ADAPTIVE ROUTING: disable entirely for Bocconi. adaptiveBehavior must be 'none'. Fixed 50-item form, fixed per-area counts, mixed difficulty ordering. Do not build a routing table, do not estimate ability, and do not label the Bocconi simulation as adaptive anywhere in copy.

SCORING: implement penalty-aware raw scoring as a config-driven rule set, not hardcoded. Undergraduate/Law: correct +1, omitted 0, incorrect -0.2, with a per-item penaltyOverride of -0.33 flagged on three-option critical-thinking items. Graduate: correct +1, omitted 0, incorrect -0.25 with a -0.33 override. Because the -0.33 override applies to an item subset Bocconi does not fully enumerate, mark any computed total as approximate whenever an item carries an unconfirmed penalty class. Report the eligibility floor (17, or 15 for graduate) as a pass/fail eligibility flag, explicitly labelled 'minimum to be considered', never as a target score.

SCORE REPORTING: mirror the real score report shape - total, per-area subtotals, and counts of correct / unanswered / incorrect. Do NOT produce a scaled score, a percentile, or an admission-chance estimate for Bocconi. The 55%/45% ranking formula may be shown as documented admissions methodology but must not be turned into a predicted-rank calculator, because GPA normalisation across school systems is undocumented.

OMISSION STRATEGY UI: since omitting costs nothing and a wrong answer costs 0.2 or 0.33, the review screen should surface an 'omitted' count as a first-class metric and explain the expected-value tradeoff. This differs sharply from the SAT, so strategy copy must be per-exam, not shared.

REQUIREMENTS DATA MODEL: key admission-requirement records by (school, level, admissionsCycle) where school is one of undergraduate-school / law-school / graduate-school. Each numeric field carries scoreClass ('official-requirement' or 'historical-statistic'), sourceUrl, sourceQuote and verificationDate. Render official-requirement values with the phrasing 'applicants below X will not be considered'. Block rendering of any historical-statistic that lacks a non-official attribution. Ship no admission-probability feature.

CYCLE FRESHNESS: Bocconi runs two cycles concurrently on its site and changes dates annually. Add a scheduled re-verification job for all Bocconi records, and have the UI display the cycle label and verification date on every deadline. Records whose cycle predates the currently-open application cycle should be visually demoted to 'past cycle' rather than silently shown.

CONTENT AUTHORING: tag the original question bank against the verified per-variant taxonomy and honour the real item counts when assembling a full simulation (undergraduate 24/11/6/9; law 5/11/6/18/10; graduate 24/16/10). Reading-comprehension items must be authored as passage_group stimuli, with economic-topic passages containing data for the undergraduate form and humanistic passages (pedagogy, history, philosophy, geography) for the law form. Do not reuse economic passages across the two forms.

FEATURES TO DISABLE PENDING VERIFICATION: any GRE cut-off display for Bocconi MSc, the per-certificate English score table beyond the B2/B1 level statement, the GRE institution code as a clickable instruction, and any claim about a Spring round for the 2027-28 Bachelor/Law cycle. Each should be gated behind a verified flag that is currently false.

TEST-DELIVERY REALISM DISCLAIMER: the real Bocconi test is remote-proctored with a lockdown browser, a mobile side camera, a 360-degree room scan and audio/video review. The platform must not imply it reproduces proctoring. Separate the three content classes the brief requires - documented Bocconi behaviour (timing, navigation, penalties, floors), our educational approximation (item content and difficulty), and not implemented (proctoring, real score reports, ranking against real applicants).
